concepts.title: Sole Proprietorship: Features, Merits and Limitations

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Sole Proprietorship: Features, Merits and Limitations' refers to.
questions.a: Sole proprietorship is a form of business owned, managed and controlled by a single individual who bears all risks, takes all profits, and has unlimited liability with no separate legal existence.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Sole Proprietorship: Features, Merits and Limitations'.
questions.a: Formation and closure are easy, secrecy is complete, and direct incentive plus quick decision making make it suitable for small scale ventures.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Sole Proprietorship: Features, Merits and Limitations' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Sole proprietorship (source: kebs102.txt sole proprietorship section)

concepts.title: Partnership: Deed, Registration, Liability and Types of Partners

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Partnership: Deed, Registration, Liability and Types of Partners' refers to.
questions.a: Partnership is the relation between persons who have agreed to share profits of a business carried on by all or any of them acting for all, governed by a partnership deed and the Partnership Act, with unlimited joint and several liability of partners.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Partnership: Deed, Registration, Liability and Types of Partners'.
questions.a: Registration is optional, and partners may be active, sleeping, secret, minor or nominal partners, with the partnership deed covering profit sharing ratio, capital, duties and dispute settlement.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Partnership: Deed, Registration, Liability and Types of Partners' taught, and from which source text?

concepts.title: Cooperative Society and Joint Stock Company

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Cooperative Society and Joint Stock Company' refers to.
questions.a: A cooperative society is a voluntary association for mutual welfare with one member one vote and service motive, while a joint stock company is an artificial person with separate legal entity, perpetual succession, common seal, limited liability and transferable shares.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Cooperative Society and Joint Stock Company'.
questions.a: The company form suits large capital needs and professional management, while cooperatives protect members from middlemen through service rather than profit motive.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Cooperative Society and Joint Stock Company' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Company (source: kebs102.txt cooperative and company sections)

concepts.title: Choice of Form of Business Organisation

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Choice of Form of Business Organisation' refers to.
questions.a: The choice among sole proprietorship, partnership, cooperative society and company depends on cost and ease of formation, liability, capital requirement, continuity, control, management ability and nature of business.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Choice of Form of Business Organisation'.
questions.a: Small ventures with limited capital suit proprietorship, growing firms take the partnership route, and large scale enterprises needing heavy investment adopt the company form.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Choice of Form of Business Organisation' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Choice of form (source: kebs102.txt choice of form section)
